title: Brand
appliesWhen: The product shows its own name, logo, colours or typefaces to users. Left out only when the product is built entirely from unbranded standard components.

paths.title: Follow an existing brand guide
paths.when: The owner or the client already has a brand guide the product must match.

paths.title: Create a new brand guide
paths.when: There is no brand guide, or the existing one is being replaced.

questions.ask: Is there a brand guide the product must follow? If yes, where is it and which version or date is current?
questions.why: Decides the path: follow the guide, or create one.

questions.ask: Does the existing guide cover screens (web or app), or only print and logo use?
questions.why: A print-only guide leaves screen decisions open; those become owner decisions, not guesses.

questions.ask: Which elements already exist and must not change: name, logo, colours, typefaces, tagline?
questions.why: Fixed elements are inputs, not design work.

questions.ask: Who is the product for, and which three words should describe how it feels to them?
questions.why: A new guide is judged against these words; without them every variation is equally right.

questions.ask: Which existing brands or products feel right, and which feel wrong?
questions.why: References show what words cannot; the wrong ones rule directions out early.

questions.ask: Which languages and scripts must the typefaces cover?
questions.why: A typeface that lacks a script the users read cannot be chosen.

questions.ask: Are there typefaces, images or icon sets already licensed, and is there a budget for new licences?
questions.why: A licence is a spend and legal decision that belongs to the owner.

criteria.mustBeTrue: The brand guide being followed is recorded with its location and its version or date.

check.how: The brand record names the guide file or link and its version or date, and the file or link opens.

criteria.mustBeTrue: Every colour value, typeface and logo file in the design tokens and logo files is the one the guide gives.

check.how: Each token value and logo file is compared with the guide, page by page; any difference is listed.

criteria.mustBeTrue: Wherever the logo is shown, the guide's clear space, minimum size and allowed backgrounds are kept.

check.how: Each placement of the logo in the rendered outputs is checked against the guide's logo rules.

criteria.mustBeTrue: Everything the product needs that the guide does not cover is listed as a decision for the owner, with a proposal for each.

check.how: The brand record has a list of uncovered items (for example dark mode, error colours, screen type sizes), each with a proposal; an empty list says so in words.

criteria.mustBeTrue: The new guide holds: the logo with its usage rules, the colour palette with a role and a value for each colour, the typefaces with a size scale, the tone of voice with examples of real product text, and the style of images or illustrations.

check.how: Each of the five parts is present in the guide and none is a placeholder.

criteria.mustBeTrue: The brand direction was chosen from at least two rendered variations, and the choice is recorded.

check.how: The variations are rendered files in the product repository and the brand record names the one chosen and when.

criteria.mustBeTrue: The guide fits the audience and the three words given in the Q&A.

check.how: The guide is read beside the Q&A answers; each of the three words is matched to something visible in the guide.

criteria.mustBeTrue: Every typeface, image and icon set the brand uses has its licence recorded, and the licence allows the product's use.

check.how: The brand record lists each asset with its licence and source; an asset with no licence line fails.

criteria.mustBeTrue: Every text and background pair listed in the design tokens file has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5 to 1 (3 to 1 for large text), in each theme.

check.how: A contrast tool measures each listed pair in each theme (WCAG 2.2, 1.4.3).

criteria.mustBeTrue: One design tokens file holds the colours with their roles, the text and background pairs that may be used together, the typefaces and the size scale.

check.how: The tokens file parses and has the colour, pair, typeface and size groups, none of them empty.

criteria.mustBeTrue: The chosen typefaces cover every language and script named in the Q&A.

check.how: A sample line in each named language is rendered in each typeface with no missing-glyph boxes.

criteria.mustBeTrue: The brand is shown to the owner on one rendered page: logo, palette, typefaces and a sample of real product text.

check.how: The page is a rendered file or published page, not a description in words.

outputs.title: Brand record
outputs.what: The guide being followed (location, version), and the list of items it does not cover with a proposal for each.

outputs.title: Brand guide
outputs.what: The new guide: logo and usage rules, colour palette with roles, typefaces and size scale, tone of voice, image style, and the licences.

outputs.title: Design tokens file
outputs.what: Colours with roles, the text and background pairs that may be used together, typefaces and the size scale, in one file the screens and the code read.

outputs.title: Logo files
outputs.what: The logo in the formats and sizes the product needs, including the small icon sizes.

outputs.title: Brand page
outputs.what: One rendered page showing the brand, for the owner to judge.

logic: A light and dark theme, when the guide has both, is a setting the product must store and apply.
assets: The design tokens file, read by the code as its only source of colours and type.
Logo files and typeface files, shipped with the product.
runtime: Each typeface file adds to the first page load; the number of typefaces and weights sets that cost.
A typeface loaded from another host is a network dependency and a privacy question.
